    Lazily encode data, params, files
    
    Previously, data, params, and files were encoded and stored in
    Request.__init__, and subsequently put into service during
    Request.send. The problem with this approach is that hooks and auth
    callables need to be aware of the eager encoding, and if they touch the
    originals, make sure to update the encoded versions.
    
    A better approach is to only encode late in the sending process. This
    way, hooks and auth callables can safely make changes without fear of
    the old, encoded variant overriding it.

    Switch LGPL'd chardet for MIT licensed charset_normalizer (#5797)
    
    Although using the (non-vendored) chardet library is fine for requests
    itself, but using a LGPL dependency the story is a lot less clear
    for downstream projects, particularly ones that might like to bundle
    requests (and thus chardet) in to a single binary -- think something
    similar to what docker-compose is doing. By including an LGPL'd module
    it is no longer clear if the resulting artefact must also be LGPL'd.
    
    By changing out this dependency for one under MIT we remove all
    license ambiguity.
    
    As an "escape hatch" I have made the code so that it will use chardet
    first if it is installed, but we no longer depend upon it directly,
    although there is a new extra added, `requests[lgpl]`. This should
    minimize the impact to users, and give them an escape hatch if
    charset_normalizer turns out to be not as good. (In my non-exhaustive
    tests it detects the same encoding as chartdet in every case I threw at
    it)

    Request.__init__, and subsequently put into service during
    Request.send. The problem with this approach is that hooks and auth
    callables need to be aware of the eager encoding, and if they touch the
    originals, make sure to update the encoded versions.

    way, hooks and auth callables can safely make changes without fear of
    the old, encoded variant overriding it.

Author: Ash Berlin-Taylor <ash_github@firemirror.com>

    Switch LGPL'd chardet for MIT licensed charset_normalizer (#5797)
    
    Although using the (non-vendored) chardet library is fine for requests
    itself, but using a LGPL dependency the story is a lot less clear
    for downstream projects, particularly ones that might like to bundle
    requests (and thus chardet) in to a single binary -- think something
    similar to what docker-compose is doing. By including an LGPL'd module
    it is no longer clear if the resulting artefact must also be LGPL'd.
    
    By changing out this dependency for one under MIT we remove all
    license ambiguity.
    
    As an "escape hatch" I have made the code so that it will use chardet
    first if it is installed, but we no longer depend upon it directly,
    although there is a new extra added, `requests[lgpl]`. This should
    minimize the impact to users, and give them an escape hatch if
    charset_normalizer turns out to be not as good. (In my non-exhaustive
    tests it detects the same encoding as chartdet in every case I threw at
    it)

I've examined the git log for commits related to "encoding". Several commits touch upon encoding detection and handling, but one stands out as directly addressing the switch of a dependency.

Commit `2ed84f55b22f19a1e1e8eea2e50963dce62052d3` states: "Switch LGPL'd chardet for MIT licensed charset_normalizer (#5797)". The commit message explains that `chardet` was replaced with `charset_normalizer` to avoid LGPL license issues for downstream projects.

The commit message also clarifies that `charset_normalizer` is used by default, but the library will still use `chardet` if it's installed, providing an escape hatch.

The commit SHA that establishes this change is `2ed84f55b22f19a1e1e8eea2e50963dce62052d3`.

Therefore, the requests library switched its default text-encoding guesser from `chardet` to `charset_normalizer` due to licensing concerns with `chardet`'s LGPL license. This change is documented in commit `2ed84f55b22f19a1e1e8eea2e50963dce62052d3`.
